messages:
Chris (Support): Nora from Acme reported repeated 429s and confusion about which quota is being enforced — org, project, API key, or IP. She says the dashboard shows plenty of headroom. Can someone help triage?

Nora (Customer): Seeing 429s across multiple endpoints since yesterday evening. Dashboard shows org usage at ~30% and project at ~20%. We only have two API keys in use. No deploys. Token: `rk-prod-...` (redacted).

Chris (Support): Thanks Nora. Can you paste a couple of failing request headers (no token) and the response body? Also whether you're coming from a static IP or NATed cloud network.

Nora (Customer): Here's a sample response: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`
```
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "detail": "key_quota_exceeded",
  "retry_after": 12
}
```
Headers (redacted):
```
Host: api.redwood.ai
X-Forwarded-For: 34.210.45.12
X-Redwood-Org: org-acme
X-Redwood-Project: project-payments
Authorization: Bearer rk-prod-REDACTED
```

June (SRE): Interesting that detail says `key_quota_exceeded` while org/project show headroom. That implies an API-key level quota or a burst window exhaustion. Two things to check: 1) per-key short-term burst limits (tokens/sec or concurrent requests) 2) IP-based throttles (we sometimes apply IP caps when many keys share same IP).

Tomas (Platform): Pinging rate-limiting config. We have layered quotas: org -> project -> key -> IP pool -> route. Dashboard defaults to 1h/24h windows for org/project; key-level burst uses sub-minute token-bucket with separate telemetry and may not surface in UI. 

Chris (Support): @Tomas can you confirm where customers can see key-level burst metrics? We should give Nora repro steps.

Tomas (Platform): Currently internal: short-term key buckets logged to `rate_limit.events` and stored for 48h. Exposing them in UI is tracked but not live yet. For repro, ask customer to: 1) run a high-frequency curl loop against the endpoint that got 429, 2) include `X-Debug-RateLimit: true` header, 3) capture `X-RateLimit-*` response headers. Example command: 
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer rk-prod-REDACTED" -H "X-Redwood-Org: org-acme" -H "X-Redwood-Project: project-payments" -H "X-Debug-RateLimit: true" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"; sleep 0.05; done
```

RepoBot: Note: rate_limit.events id=rl_ev_9843 recorded for org-acme at 2025-11-12T22:14:01Z (key_quota_exceeded).

Priyanka (Account): Nora — quick question: are you using a gateway/proxy (Cloudflare, APIM, ngrok) that might be sharing an IP across many services? That would trigger IP-pool caps. Also any recent SDK rollout?

Nora (Customer): We're behind a corporate NAT. Only 12 dev machines but several CI runners use same NAT. No cloud proxy. We do have a scheduled bulk job that calls embeddings every 15 minutes, but it's modest.

June (SRE): Two parallel hypotheses: 1) a bursty job (CI or bulk) is hitting per-key short windows, or 2) your NAT causes an IP pool throttle. To distinguish: can you run the same curl loop from a machine with a different public IP (phone hotspot)? If 429s disappear, it's IP-pool. If they persist and the `detail` stays `key_quota_exceeded`, then it's key-bucket.

Chris (Support): Also Nora, add a header `X-Request-ID: local-test-123` so we can correlate logs on our side and I'll escalate to infra if needed.

Nora (Customer): Ran quick hotspot test — from phone hotspot, the same loop returned 200s for all requests. From office NAT, 429s start around iteration 37. Attached two raw captures (redacted).

Tomas (Platform): That strongly indicates IP-pool throttle. We track an IP pool quota that protects shared infra — it's enforced before per-key buckets. The error `key_quota_exceeded` can be emitted if the key was used from a blackholed IP pool, misleading but historically a compatibility artifact. We'll fix message mapping, but immediate fix options below.

June (SRE): Immediate mitigations: 1) Short term: ask you to switch CI runners to use distinct egress IPs or stagger retries; 2) We can create a temporary IP exception for your NAT (requires ticket + A record check); 3) Use a dedicated API gateway with static egress assigned to a Dedicated capacity if you need consistent high QPS.

Priyanka (Account): Nora — if you want us to request an IP exception, paste the public IP(s) and confirm the business case (CI and dev traffic). I'll open an internal request to Platform for a 72-hour IP whitelist.

Nora (Customer): Public IP: 34.210.45.12. Business case: CI runners + dev machines, need stable throughput for test runs. Please proceed with temporary exception.

Chris (Support): Done — opened internal ticket INF-3921 and attached your captures + `local-test-123`. @Tomas can you review INF-3921 for IP whitelist and also adjust error mapping so `key_quota_exceeded` vs `ip_pool_exceeded` is clearer?

Tomas (Platform): Looking at INF-3921. Quick notes for the whitelist flow: we validate ownership, then add to the IP exception table for 72 hours and monitor. Post-whitelist, we still enforce key-level bursts. We'll also add a telemetry change to emit `X-RateLimit-Source` header in debug mode showing which layer tripped. Estimate for header rollout to beta: 2 weeks.

June (SRE): For long-term: recommend using per-environment API keys (one for CI, one for dev), and enable exponential backoff + jitter in CI retries. Also consider Dedicated if you need guaranteed concurrent throughput. I'll post a short doc snippet with recommended token bucket params and recommended retry strategy.

RepoBot: INF-3921 state: assigned -> platform -> waiting for IP verification.

Chris (Support): Nora — temporary whitelist requested. In parallel, could you: 1) create a separate API key for CI, 2) add `X-Tag: ci-run` header so we can track CI traffic separately, 3) implement backoff with jitter per the snippet June will share. That will reduce chance of hitting key-level bursts after whitelist is removed.

Nora (Customer): Will do. Thanks everyone. One last question — what about auth edge case where we rotate keys via a proxy and the `Authorization` header gets replaced by a proxy token? Could that cause mis-attribution?

Tomas (Platform): Yes — if an edge proxy swaps the bearer token or injects an API key in a different header, we may attribute requests to a different key or the `unknown` bucket, which can hit default conservative limits. Recommend: ensure proxy preserves original `Authorization` or forwards original key in `X-Original-Auth`. We can also add support to accept an `X-Forwarded-Api-Key` header behind authenticated internal proxies, but that requires an enterprise config.

June (SRE): Also watch for auth caching at the proxy layer — stale cached auth can route traffic under a deactivated key which will 403 rather than 429, but some proxies retry with alternate keys causing mixed attribution. If you see mixed `detail` values (`forbidden` vs `key_quota_exceeded`), check proxy token rotation logs.

Priyanka (Account): I'll follow up once IP whitelist is approved. @Nora please DM me once you create the CI key.

Nora (Customer): CI key created, header `X-Tag: ci-run` added, switching CI egress to staggered windows. Confirming my public IP posted. Thanks team!

Chris (Support): Closing loop for now — INF-3921 will track the whitelist; follow up if 429s persist after whitelist. Leaving action items: Platform to add clearer error mapping and debug header (Tomas), SRE to publish retry/backoff snippet (June), Account to manage whitelist request (Priyanka).

Tomas (Platform): Note to self: create a follow-up ticket to expose short-bucket metrics in console and emit `X-RateLimit-Source` on debug.

RepoBot: INF-3921 updated: platform approved provisional whitelist for 34.210.45.12 for 72h.

Chris (Support): Resolved status: monitoring. Thanks all :thumbsup:.
